001.title: Paper Verse
001.subtitle: Science Library Design, Sichuan University
001.description:
Centered on the concept of Paper Verse, this project creates an open engineering library that brings reading, research, and exchange together. A concrete base establishes the building’s material character, while vertical curtain-wall fins evoke the texture of turning pages and produce soft, diffused daylight.

The basement contains book storage and a lecture hall for collections and academic events. On the ground floor, an open lobby connects exhibition and training spaces, dissolving conventional boundaries around knowledge. Reading and seminar areas occupy the second and third floors, where double-height voids strengthen spatial continuity. Above, an ETFE-covered sky garden combines a café, sensory gardens, and leisure paths to form a restorative public landscape. Stairs and ramps weave the programs into a continuous sequence in which reading, conversation, and nature coexist, responding to both the campus context and its ecological needs.

002.title: WEAVING STRATA
002.subtitle: Vertical Ground Reconstruction and Urban Interface Restoration
002.description:
Set within Chengdu’s high-density urban context, the proposal responds to the fragmented city fabric produced by conventional gated superblocks. It rethinks the usual opposition between public and private space and explores a three-dimensional open neighborhood that combines civic permeability with a clear sense of territory.

The scheme introduces a vertically layered system. At ground level, the buildings are lifted to release a continuous urban surface. This highly permeable threshold reduces the visual weight of the towers and extends street life inward through commercial frontages, softening the physical boundary between private plots and public streets.

A continuous elevated walkway forms the community’s second ground. By separating pedestrians from bicycles, deliveries, and service traffic below, it creates a safe and uninterrupted slow-mobility network. The red walkway operates as both infrastructure and a social condenser, linking shared resting places across the buildings and framing views toward the waterfront. Through this spatial repair, the project restores a human scale for everyday encounters while reconnecting the residential district to the city’s ongoing growth.

003.title: Pura Haven
003.subtitle: Urban Resort Hotel Design through Environmental Interaction
003.description:
This urban resort hotel is located beside the Jin River and Wangjianglou Park in Chengdu. Drawing on the city’s cultural setting and waterfront landscape, it creates a quiet place of retreat within the urban center.

Guided by the idea of simple dwelling in harmony with its surroundings, the design responds to wind and daylight conditions to refine the building layout and guest-room orientation, maximizing views of the river and greenery. Transparent façades, a swimming pool, and landscaped paths connect spaces for rest, social life, and contact with nature. With a restrained presence in the city fabric, the hotel offers travelers a resort experience grounded in both local character and everyday comfort.

004.title: Anxi Museum of Braiding and Fishing
004.subtitle: Rural Settlement Conservation and Renewal Design
004.description:
The project takes Anxi’s intangible cultural heritage—rope braiding and fishing traditions—as the foundation for a rural museum of preservation, exhibition, and participation. Linear volumes are stretched, shifted, and layered in response to the existing settlement pattern, linking galleries, workshops, and public rooms into an open but ordered spatial sequence.

Concrete, stone cladding, and peach wood define the façades. Their rough, restrained, and warm textures translate the material language of the countryside and allow the building to settle gently into the fields. Inside, intersecting walls and corridors draw from the structure of knots, producing a layered route that leads visitors from exhibitions to working studios and into the living history of local craft.

The site plan retains the surrounding agricultural grain. Walking and cycling paths connect the entrance square, parking areas, and museum while limiting the impact of vehicles on the village environment. Sheltered edges and landscape paths extend cultural activity beyond the galleries, giving residents and visitors places to rest and meet.

The museum is conceived not only as a container for heritage but also as a catalyst for rural life. By translating traditional skills through a contemporary architectural language, it brings the memory of braiding and fishing back into everyday life and supports a renewed public identity for Anxi.
